title: Dev-provisioned peers keyed by hwid EUI-64, not canonical SHA-512(pubkey) - SIID key selection always misses
description: Wave review of jfln (SIID-indexed key selection) found: the new comment in lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lichen_l2_peer.c:113-128 claims trust-store entries are keyed by canonical key-derived EUI-64, but the only in-tree populator (dev_provision_peer, lichen_l2_dev.c:62-82) keys entries by CONFIG_LICHEN_L2_DEV_PEER_EUI64 (board/hwid form), while wire SIID is SHA-512(pubkey)[0:8] | U/L. On every dev-provisioned build peer_find_locked(parsed.signer_iid) misses and ALL signed frames reject -EAUTH. Same outcome as the old trial-verify (binding gate rejected them too), so not a regression, but the wave enshrines an unenforced invariant and the new 'unknown SIID rejected' log misleads field debugging (the peer IS pinned, under a different key form). Fix options: enforce canonical keying at pin time in lichen_peer_add (SHA-512 of pubkey, memcmp vs key arg) or key dev provisioning by the canonical form. No announce/EDHOC populator exists in-tree yet.
